findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update evaluates the stored IdP through the org-aware wrapper
findings.body: update() obtains `idpById` via getById() (line 91), which returns the model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization (or the OrganizationProvider) is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then runs getLoginPredicate() on this wrapper, but the login caches were built from raw DB rows where org state is irrelevant. Consequence: for an enabled, public IdP linked to a disabled org, an update that makes it not login-eligible (e.g. setHideOnLogin(true) or setLinkOnly(true)) gives test(original)=false and test(updated)=false, so no invalidation is registered. The cached ALL/ORG_ONLY lists still contain the IdP id. The consumer (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly, and enabling an org does not invalidate login caches. Once the org is re-enabled, the hidden IdP is shown on the login page. The original state should be taken from the raw stored model (not the org-aware wrapper) before evaluating the predicate.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", so the 20 IdPs created in testCacheIDPForLogin leak
findings.body: The cleanup `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (copied from the pre-existing testCacheIDPByOrg) never references the IdP that was created (`"idp-alias-" + i`). The 20 IdPs therefore remain in the realm after the test, and 10 of them (idp-alias-10..19) stay linked to orga. testCacheIDPByOrg asserts exact membership counts for orga (e.g. 6) and the new test asserts exact login counts, so their results depend on JUnit method execution order and can fail once the other runs first. The cleanup should reference the created alias.

findings.title: Cache search key conflates null and "" organizationId, which the delegate treats differently
findings.body: searchKey maps both null and "" to "". The delegate's default getForLogin only adds the ORGANIZATION_ID filter when organizationId != null. With null, ORG_ONLY/ALL return IdPs of any organization. With "", it adds an explicit ORGANIZATION_ID="" filter with different results. Because both share the same cache slot, a result computed for one input can be served for the other. Use a key that distinguishes null from the empty string.

findings.title: remove() now always performs a DB lookup of the IdP
findings.body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was moved out of the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch, so every remove() now issues an extra DB query even when the alias entry is served from cache. The result is needed only for the new login invalidation and for the invalid branch. The lookup could be deferred or the cached model could be used for the login check.

findings.title: No test covers invalidation when a login-eligible IdP is created or removed
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates a hidden IdP (line 424) and removes a disabled IdP (line 428). Both are paths where login caches must NOT be invalidated. The new registerIDPLoginInvalidation calls in create() and remove() for IdPs that are actually login-eligible are never exercised, so a regression there would go unnoticed. Also untested is the scenario where an org-linked IdP's login eligibility changes while its organization is disabled, which is where the wrapper-based classification in update() goes wrong.
